
# Align-fastqs test fixtures
These fixtures are synthetic micro-fixtures for fast, deterministic tests of the align-fastqs workflow.

They are intentionally small and hand-checkable. Running `make.sh` from `env_protocol` regenerates the fixture set deterministically.

Regenerate fixtures from the repository root with:
```bash
source activate env_protocol
bash tests/fixtures/align_fastqs/make.sh
```

Generated fixture outputs are ignored by Git. When required inputs are missing, `tests/run_tests.sh` regenerates this fixture set automatically.

The fixture set focuses on single-end and paired-end Bowtie2 alignment to BAM and CRAM output, plus BWA MEM, BWA ALN, and bwa-mem2 MEM alignment to BAM output. These fixtures are not derived from real sequencing data. The reference sequence and FASTQ records are encoded directly in `make.sh` so that the expected read alignments are easy to inspect.

<br />

- `reference/tiny.fa`

## Expected alignment behavior
The single-end FASTQ fixture contains one read:

| Read name        | Sequence                         | Expected reference |
| :---             | :---                             | :---               |
| `tiny_se_read_1` | `ACGTTGACCGTTAACGATCGTAGCTAGGAT` | `I`                |

Bowtie2, BWA MEM, BWA ALN, and bwa-mem2 MEM should align this read to chromosome `I` in the tiny reference. Tests should verify that wrapper-generated BAM/CRAM files and indexes exist, pass `samtools quickcheck`, report or count one read alignment on `I`, and contain the expected read name. CRAM checks should read with `samtools view -T reference/tiny.fa`.

The paired-end FASTQ fixtures contain one read pair:

| Read name        | Mate | Sequence                         | Expected reference | Expected start |
| :---             | :--- | :---                             | :---               | :---           |
| `tiny_pe_pair_1` | R1   | `ACGTTGACCGTTAACGATCGTAGCTAGGAT` | `I`                | 17             |
| `tiny_pe_pair_1` | R2   | `CCTTAGCCGATTAGCCTAAGCTTGATCCGG` | `I`                | 70             |

R1 matches chromosome `I` in forward orientation. R2 is the reverse complement of positions 70-99 on chromosome `I`, so Bowtie2, BWA MEM, BWA ALN, and bwa-mem2 MEM should report the pair in FR orientation. Tests should verify that wrapper-generated BAM/CRAM files and indexes exist, pass `samtools quickcheck`, report or count two read alignments on `I`, contain the expected paired read name, and include proper-pair flag records when the aligner reports stable proper-pair flags. CRAM checks should read with `samtools view -T reference/tiny.fa`.

<br />

### Repeat fixtures
`make.sh` writes one 150-base repeat and four 400-base unique blocks literally, then joins them into the 2,050-base reference `chrR`: the unique blocks separated by three copies of the repeat. A read wholly in the repeat therefore has three equally good placements. The 100-base reads are cut from the blocks:

| Read name | R1                                            | R2     | In single-end input |
| :---      | :---                                          | :---   | :---                |
| `chim`    | 60 bases of repeat, then 40 of unique block 3 | unique | yes                 |
| `rchm`    | 60 bases of unique block 3, then 40 of repeat | unique | yes                 |
| `half`    | wholly in the repeat                          | unique | no                  |
| `ctrl`    | unique                                        | unique | yes                 |

With BWA MEM and bwa-mem2, `chim` R1 is a split read with its primary in the repeat, `rchm` R1 a split read with its supplementary in the repeat, and `half` a pair whose mates get different MAPQ; BWA ALN gives `half` different mate MAPQs too. Bowtie2 writes no supplementary records. `test_align_fastqs_mapq_template.sh` checks the MAPQs each aligner writes before relying on them.

In the SAM fixtures, template `sec_keep` has primary records at MAPQ 60 and a secondary record at MAPQ 0, and `sec_drop` has a primary record at MAPQ 0 and a secondary record at MAPQ 255. Filtered at MAPQ 30 by primary records, only `sec_keep` is kept, with its secondary record.

<br />

## Current and deferred test coverage
The test suite covers submit- and execute-layer single-end and paired-end alignment, a local Bowtie2 GNU Parallel path gated by `RUN_PARALLEL=1`, and a remote Slurm submission path gated by `RUN_SLURM=1`. Set `WAIT_SLURM=1` with `RUN_SLURM=1` to poll for expected Slurm outputs.

`#TODO`: Consider extending GNU Parallel coverage to additional aligners and CRAM output where that broader matrix provides useful regression protection.
